name: Vancouver
tagline: A genuinely rare city where snow-capped mountains, old-growth forest and the Pacific Ocean all sit within view of downtown skyscrapers.
highlight: Cycling the Stanley Park seawall at golden hour, downtown's glass towers on one side and the Coast Mountains rising straight from the water on the other.
shortDescription: A genuinely rare city where mountains, forest and ocean all meet downtown, home to Stanley Park, Granville Island and some of North America's best Asian food.
metaDescription: A Vancouver travel guide: Stanley Park, Granville Island, the Capilano Suspension Bridge, Gastown, food and how to plan a visit to Canada's West Coast city.
knownFor: Stanley Park, Granville Island, mountains meeting the sea

image.alt: Vancouver's skyline against the Coast Mountains

intro: Vancouver is genuinely one of the few cities anywhere where mountains, old-growth forest and the Pacific Ocean all sit within sight of downtown skyscrapers.
Its layout genuinely rewards being outside as much as in a restaurant or museum — Stanley Park's seawall, Granville Island's market and North Shore mountain trails all sit an easy trip from the core.
The city's genuinely large Asian population has also made it one of North America's best food cities outside Asia itself, with dim sum, sushi and fusion dishes found at every price point.

whyVisit.intro: Vancouver's case rests genuinely on a setting that pairs a real, livable city with immediate access to mountains and ocean.

points.title: The setting is genuinely unmatched in North America
points.text: Ocean, old-growth forest and snow-capped mountains all visible from downtown.

points.title: Stanley Park is genuinely one of the great urban parks
points.text: Old-growth forest and a seawall right at the edge of the downtown core.

points.title: The food scene is genuinely world class
points.text: A large Asian population has made Vancouver one of the best cities in North America for dim sum and sushi.

points.title: The mountains are genuinely a short trip away
points.text: Grouse Mountain and the North Shore's trails sit a quick drive or gondola ride from downtown.

points.title: It works genuinely well as a Western Canada gateway
points.text: An easy pairing with Whistler and, further on, the Rockies via Calgary.

attractionsIntro: Vancouver's essential sights are genuinely spread between its downtown core and the nature right at its edges.

attractions.name: Stanley Park's totem poles

image.file: File:Vancouver (BC, Canada), Stanley Park, Totem poles -- 2022 -- 2045.jpg
image.alt: Totem poles in Stanley Park, Vancouver

attractions.text: Genuinely one of the park's most visited spots, a collection of carved First Nations totem poles overlooking the harbour.
attractions.tip: Genuinely read the accompanying plaques for context on each pole's origin and meaning.

attractions.name: Granville Island Public Market

image.alt: Granville Island Public Market in Vancouver

attractions.text: Genuinely a lively covered market under the Granville Street Bridge, stalls selling produce, seafood and crafts.
attractions.tip: Genuinely arrive hungry — the food stalls here are genuinely excellent for a casual lunch.

attractions.name: Capilano Suspension Bridge

image.alt: The Capilano Suspension Bridge near Vancouver

attractions.text: Genuinely a thrilling walk, a 137-metre suspension bridge swaying 70 metres above the Capilano River canyon.
attractions.tip: Genuinely continue on to the treetop walkways beyond the bridge for more of the same forest canopy views.

attractions.name: Gastown's Steam Clock

image.alt: The Steam Clock in Gastown, Vancouver

attractions.text: Genuinely the centrepiece of Vancouver's oldest neighbourhood, a steam-powered clock that whistles every 15 minutes.
attractions.tip: Genuinely time your visit for the top of the hour, when the whistle plays a longer tune.

attractions.name: English Bay Beach
attractions.text: Genuinely the city's favourite sunset spot, a curving downtown beach backed by palm-lined Denman Street.
attractions.tip: Genuinely arrive an hour before sunset to grab a spot on the sand or the seawall.

attractions.name: Grouse Mountain

image.file: File:Vancouver from Grouse Mountain at dusk.jpg
image.alt: Vancouver seen from Grouse Mountain at dusk

attractions.text: Genuinely known as 'the Peak of Vancouver', a gondola-accessible mountain with sweeping city and ocean views.
attractions.tip: Genuinely check for the resident grizzly bears at the mountain's wildlife refuge.

attractions.name: The downtown skyline
attractions.text: Genuinely striking from almost any angle, glass towers rising directly against a backdrop of mountains and water.
attractions.tip: Genuinely the best views come from the water itself, via a short ferry or harbour cruise.

thingsToDoIntro: Vancouver genuinely rewards splitting time between its downtown neighbourhoods and easy access to nature.

thingsToDo.title: Walk or cycle the Stanley Park seawall

image.file: File:Vancouver (BC, Canada), Stanley Park, Totem poles -- 2022 -- 2033.jpg

thingsToDo.text: A genuinely essential Vancouver experience, a flat, scenic path circling the entire park along the waterfront.
thingsToDo.tip: Genuinely rent a bike near the park entrance rather than trying to walk the full 10-kilometre loop.

thingsToDo.title: Browse Granville Island's market stalls

image.alt: Market stalls at Granville Island in Vancouver

thingsToDo.text: A genuinely relaxed way to spend a morning, sampling fresh produce, seafood and baked goods.
thingsToDo.tip: Genuinely catch the small Aquabus ferry across False Creek for a scenic way to arrive.

thingsToDo.title: Cross the Capilano Suspension Bridge
thingsToDo.text: A genuinely memorable half-day trip, walking the swaying bridge and forest canopy walkways above the canyon.
thingsToDo.tip: Genuinely book tickets online ahead to skip the entrance queue in peak season.

thingsToDo.title: Wander Gastown and see the Steam Clock strike
thingsToDo.text: A genuinely easy way to spend an afternoon, cobblestone streets lined with boutiques, galleries and restaurants.
thingsToDo.tip: Genuinely explore beyond the Steam Clock itself — Gastown's side streets hold the neighbourhood's real character.

thingsToDo.title: Ride the gondola up Grouse Mountain

image.file: File:North Vancouver from Grouse Mountain - panoramio.jpg
image.alt: The view from Grouse Mountain over North Vancouver

thingsToDo.text: A genuinely rewarding half-day trip, trading the city for alpine trails and sweeping views in minutes.
thingsToDo.tip: Genuinely check for lumberjack shows and wildlife exhibits included with your gondola ticket.

thingsToDo.title: Relax at English Bay Beach
thingsToDo.text: A genuinely easy, low-key way to end a day, watching the sunset with the city's beach volleyball crowd.
thingsToDo.tip: Genuinely grab food from nearby Denman Street to enjoy on the sand.

foodIntro: Vancouver's food genuinely rivals any city in North America for Asian cuisine, alongside fresh Pacific seafood.

foods.name: Fresh Pacific salmon
foods.text: Genuinely a Pacific Northwest staple, wild salmon appearing on menus across every price point.
foods.whereToTry: Restaurants throughout downtown and Granville Island.

foods.name: Dim sum

image.file: File:Three dim sum in steamer basket.jpg
image.alt: Dim sum, small steamed dishes popular in Vancouver

foods.text: Genuinely some of the best outside Asia itself, a legacy of Vancouver's large Chinese community.
foods.whereToTry: Restaurants throughout the city, especially in Richmond, a short transit ride away.

foods.name: Japadog
foods.text: Genuinely a Vancouver original, hot dogs topped with Japanese ingredients like teriyaki sauce and seaweed.

foods.name: Nanaimo bars

image.alt: A Nanaimo bar, a layered dessert originating in British Columbia

foods.text: Genuinely a local classic, named for the British Columbia town where the no-bake dessert originated.

foods.name: Poutine

image.alt: Poutine, Canada's fries, cheese curds and gravy dish

foods.text: Genuinely widely available, though this is Quebec's dish rather than a local specialty.
foods.whereToTry: Restaurants and food trucks throughout the city.

foods.name: British Columbia craft beer
foods.text: Genuinely a thriving local scene, with breweries scattered throughout East Vancouver and beyond.
foods.whereToTry: Craft breweries and taprooms throughout the city.

accommodation.intro: Vancouver genuinely offers accommodation for every budget, with downtown commanding the highest prices.

areas.name: Downtown or the West End
areas.bestFor: Being genuinely within walking distance of Stanley Park and the main sights
areas.text: The most convenient, though also the priciest, part of the city to stay.

areas.name: Gastown or Mount Pleasant
areas.bestFor: A genuinely more character-filled, slightly better value stay
areas.text: A short transit ride from downtown, with their own restaurant and bar scenes.

gettingThere.intro: Vancouver is genuinely well connected internationally, with its airport a short trip from downtown.

options.text: Genuinely available from across North America, Asia and Europe.
options.detail: The Canada Line SkyTrain connects the airport to downtown in about 25 minutes.

options.text: Genuinely straightforward for those already in the US Pacific Northwest.
options.detail: About three hours by road, depending on border wait times.

options.mode: Via Rail or drive from the Rockies
options.text: Genuinely a scenic option for those continuing on from Whistler or Banff.
options.detail: The Rocky Mountaineer offers a luxury scenic rail option between the coast and the mountains.

gettingAround.intro: Vancouver's genuinely compact downtown is walkable, with SkyTrain and buses covering the wider city well.

options.text: Genuinely fast, frequent and easy to use across the metro area.
options.detail: A single fare system covers trains and buses throughout Vancouver and its suburbs.

options.text: Genuinely the best way to explore downtown and Stanley Park.
options.detail: Bike share stations are widely available throughout the core.

options.text: Genuinely a fun, scenic way to reach Granville Island.
options.detail: Small passenger ferries run frequently across False Creek.

bestTime.headline: June to September for warm, dry weather
bestTime.summary: Vancouver is genuinely famous for rain, with summer offering a real, sunny exception to that reputation.

seasons.text: Genuinely warm and dry, the best season for the seawall, beaches and mountain day trips.
Genuinely still pleasant, with fall colour in the parks and noticeably fewer visitors than summer.
Genuinely wet and grey downtown, though nearby ski resorts make the most of mountain snow.
Genuinely a mild shoulder season, with cherry blossoms a real citywide highlight in April.

bestTime.avoid: Genuinely the wettest winter months if outdoor sightseeing is your priority.

itinerary.title: Three days in Vancouver
itinerary.intro: Built around Stanley Park, Granville Island and a half-day in the North Shore mountains.

days.title: Downtown and Stanley Park
days.summary: The city's core and its famous park.
days.afternoon: Cycle the Stanley Park seawall and see the totem poles.

days.title: Granville Island and the North Shore
days.summary: A market morning and mountain afternoon.

days.title: Grouse Mountain
days.summary: A final day in the mountains above the city.
days.morning: Ride the gondola up Grouse Mountain.
days.afternoon: Explore the mountain's trails and wildlife refuge.

tipsIntro: Practical notes that make a Vancouver visit noticeably smoother.
tips: Pack genuinely a light rain jacket, even in summer — weather can shift quickly.
Book genuinely the Capilano Suspension Bridge online ahead in peak season.
Rent genuinely a bike for the Stanley Park seawall rather than attempting the full loop on foot.
Take genuinely the Aquabus to Granville Island for a more scenic arrival than walking.
Try genuinely dim sum in Richmond for some of the best outside Asia itself.
Use genuinely Vancouver as a base for day trips to Whistler or the wider Sea to Sky corridor.

faq.q: How many days do you need in Vancouver?
faq.a: Three days genuinely covers the city's essential sights, including a half-day trip into the North Shore mountains.
Genuinely one of Canada's pricier cities, particularly for accommodation, though food covers every budget.

faq.q: Does it rain a lot in Vancouver?
faq.a: Genuinely yes in winter, though summer is reliably warm and dry — plan accordingly.
Yes, genuinely — its large Asian population makes it one of North America's best cities for dim sum, sushi and fusion cuisine.

faq.q: Do you need a car in Vancouver?
faq.a: No, genuinely not for the city itself — SkyTrain and buses cover it well, though a car helps for reaching Whistler.

faq.q: Can you combine Vancouver with Whistler or the Rockies?
faq.a: Yes, genuinely easily — Whistler is a scenic two-hour drive, and Banff is reachable via a short flight to Calgary.
